title: opentoline
summary: Open a file to a requested editor line in MATLAB-compatible code.

gpu_support.notes: Host-side editor navigation request. gpuArray scalar position inputs are gathered before validation.

description: `opentoline(filename,line)` resolves a file and validates a host-safe editor-navigation request. RunMat runtimes are noninteractive, so successful calls complete without launching an editor.
behaviors: `opentoline(filename,line)` accepts a string scalar, row character vector, or scalar string array filename plus a positive integer line number.
`opentoline(filename,line,column)` also validates a positive integer column number.
`opentoline(filename,line,column,'select')` accepts MATLAB-style selection intent as a no-op navigation option in noninteractive hosts.
Command-style numeric line and column arguments passed as text, such as `opentoline file.m 10 4`, are accepted when they parse as positive integers.
File names are resolved using the RunMat search path and the same general MATLAB-style file extensions used by `open`.
Non-scalar, nonfinite, fractional, zero, or negative line and column values raise `RunMat:opentoline:InvalidPosition`.

faqs.question: Does `opentoline` launch a desktop editor?
faqs.answer: No. RunMat's runtime implementation is host-safe and noninteractive. It resolves the file and validates the requested position; the actual editor navigation completes as a no-op.

faqs.question: Why is this builtin under `io/repl_fs` instead of plotting?
faqs.answer: `opentoline` is an editor/file navigation helper. It appeared in a plotting/UI token bucket, but its runtime ownership belongs with REPL-facing filesystem and editor-style operations.

gpu_behavior: `opentoline` is a host-side editor navigation operation and does not participate in GPU fusion or provider-native execution.
